category_title: Middle school student with cerebral palsy and orthopedic impairment exhibiting self-injurious behavior and verbal outbursts
minimal_context: Jason is sitting in a general education classroom with an unfamiliar tutor to read an article about the culture of Japan and identify letters.
dialogue:
TUTOR: We are going to read this article about the culture of Japan today. Can you look at the page and identify the first letter for me?

STUDENT: (Turns his head away, refusing to talk or interact with the unfamiliar tutor.)

TUTOR: Please look at the article. What letter is this right here?

STUDENT: (Continues refusing to talk and begins engaging in self-stimulation, flapping his hands and rocking his body.)

TUTOR: You need to try to answer. Just point to the letter on the paper.

STUDENT: (Lets out a loud verbal outburst and begins engaging in self-injurious behavior, hitting himself and picking at his skin.)

options.A: Ask the student to describe the visual form of the letters printed in the article during the activity.
options.B: Prompt teachers and classmates to ask questions to elicit verbal or nonverbal responses about the article.
options.C: Provide direct verbal encouragement and positive reinforcement during the activity, telling him, 'Don't say you can't, you can.'
options.D: Offer diverse genres on relevant topics about Japan from which he can choose, including graphic novels, poetry, and biographies.
